## Open

### T-699 — Build the signal registry with wildcard policy overrides

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · open_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

`src/registry.ts`: one entry per declared method holding the declaration, the effective policy and
the counters (reached, emitted, sampled out, suppressed); `patch()` merges overrides at runtime; a
namespace key (`agent`) matches every identifier that begins with it, an exact key wins over its
namespace, and the identifier itself is the one the counters and the report use. The effective
policy is computed on read so hot reload needs no re-declaration.

- verify: a unit test patches a level while a call sequence is running and sees the new level on the
  next call.

### T-700 — Capture the call site at property access and record the dependency edge

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · open_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

`src/proxy.ts`: the vocabulary object is a `Proxy` whose `get` returns a callable for an enabled
entry and `undefined` for a disabled one. The trap captures the first stack frame outside lukaot and
the runtime (`src/`, `core/blong-gogo/src/`), keeping `{file, line,     function}` with
`captureStack` false meaning file and line only, and records the file-to-method edge once per
(proxy, method). Memoise per proxy so repeated access is free.

- verify: a unit test asserts two calls from one line report one site and the dependency map lists
  that file against that method; a timing test asserts a disabled method costs no capture.

### T-701 — Emit a record from a log signal with its parameters and identity

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · open_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

`src/emit.ts`: build the record from the declaration, the call's params, the captured site and the
ambient identity; interpolate `{placeholder}` with the declared message, marking a value that did
not arrive as `?name?`. Level is the effective policy's, sampling is decided once per call, and the
shape counters are updated whether or not the record is retained.

- verify: a unit test asserts identity, level, params and site on a record, and that a sampled out
  call increments `sampledOut` without reaching the writer.

### T-702 — Emit a typed error signal that records once and honours `silent`

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · open_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

`src/error.ts`: constructing an error signal returns the `ITypedError`-shaped object the gateway,
the expected-error matcher and the completion handler already understand — `type`, `message`,
`print`, `params`, `statusCode`, `validation`, `silent` — and records it at the declaration's level
in the same call. `silent` suppresses the record by default and stays overridable by policy. A
`cause` is carried through and rendered compactly.

- verify: a unit test asserts one call produces one error value and one record, and that a `silent`
  signal produces the value and no record.

### T-703 — Allow a vocabulary to be declared imperatively at assembly time

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · open_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

`declare()` is callable from code, not only from a layer file: a `library()` computing its keys and
a handler group declaring inline both register into the same per-realm registry under the same
names, so a method declared in code is indistinguishable from one declared in `lukaot/signal.ts`. A
duplicate name is refused with both declaration sites named. There is no counterpart for emission —
nothing in lukaot builds a signal out of a message.

- verify: a unit test declares from a `library()` and asserts the method reaches the realm's proxy
  and the same policy; a second declaration of one name fails naming both sites.

### T-704 — Keep a compatibility logger for the packages that still call levels

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · open_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

`src/compat.ts` implements `ILog`/`ILogger` over lukaot by _declaring_ on first use: a tuple of
namespace, level and message becomes a single-token signal — `legacy` plus the namespace plus the
message's leading words in PascalCase (`legacyChatCannotVerifyTheToken`), with a short hash appended
when two messages reduce to one token — declared imperatively and marked `legacy: true` in its
policy. A package that has not been swept yet therefore has identity, policy and retention with no
hashing, masking or stack capture, and a call site that keeps printing the same sentence keeps one
identity. `lukaot legacy` lists every such signal with the package that produced it — the work order
for the follow-ups, which shrinks to empty without the API changing.

- verify: a unit test asserts two identical calls declare one signal, a differing message declares a
  second, and `legacy` lists both against their package.

### T-705 — Port identity, capability, progress points and the call channel into lukaot

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · open_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

Move `context.ts`, `propagation.ts`, `capability.ts`, `decide.ts`, `refs.ts`, `level.ts`,
`cache.ts`, `retention.ts` and `logger.ts` from `semantic-log`, renaming `mintRecordRef` to the
`lukaot://` scheme and dropping the hash fingerprint (`fingerprint.ts`) in favour of the signal
identity. The renderer and the writers are re-hosted on pino in the transport task, so no text
formatting stays here. Keep the `attach…` facade: a browser bundle must still reach identity without
importing `node:async_hooks`.

- verify: the ported unit tests pass in `core/lukaot`, including the degraded-facade test.

### T-706 — Write through pino, and keep the coloured human line beside it

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · open_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

`src/transport.ts`: an emitted record becomes one pino call at its effective level, so the JSON
format, the transports and pino's own serialisers are pino's business; the coloured human line
`semantic-log` prints today is kept as its formatter, with field order and styling unchanged.
`pino-cacache` moves in beside it as the retention transport, and the store keeps one entry per
**signal** plus a per-emit entry where folding would hide a withheld payload or an error. `inspect`
resolves one `lukaot://` reference in compact, detailed or machine-readable form.

- verify: `cd core/lukaot && blong-dev test` asserts the human line against a golden string, the
  JSON mode against a parsed record, and that `inspect` resolves a reference after the writing
  process exits.

### T-698 — Declare the signal vocabulary and infer each method's parameters

> _2026-11-18 · core/lukaot · done_

Planned in `plans/lukaot/plan.md`.

`declare({log, error})` in `src/declare.ts`: string shorthand is an error with only a message, an
object is either kind by the keys it carries, an unknown key is rejected at declaration with the key
named, and an identifier carrying a dot or any other character that is not part of a camelCase token
is refused too, because the identity has to be one searchable word. The return type maps each
declared identifier to its method and types the parameters from the `{placeholder}` names of
`message`; the `?name?` spelling a realm writes today is accepted and normalised into the same
parameter set, because `realm/blong-agent` declares 14 of them and the framework has never
interpolated that form. `statusCode`, `print`, `silent`, `level` and `sample` are per-entry
defaults.

- verify: a type test asserts a call with a missing placeholder fails `tsc`, and a unit test asserts
  an undeclared key is refused with its name in the message, as is `'agent.ticket'`.

src/declare.ts: identifier grammar, ?name? normalisation, per-kind defaults, duplicate and
unknown-kind refusal; SignalParams/SignalVocabulary types with a @ts-expect-error
missing-placeholder check; 22 assertions green
